items.entity: MBB supports: symmetry edge and right-end support location
items.description: Appendix C only says 'standard MBB beam boundary conditions [17]' with the load at the top-left node; no restrained nodes/DOFs are listed and no BC figure exists. That the 144x48 mesh is the symmetric half-beam (u_x=0 along the left edge, support at the bottom-right end) is inferred from the reference and load position, never stated.
readings: Left edge (x=0): u_x=0 at every node (symmetry plane); right support at the single bottom-right corner node (x=L, y=0)
Left edge: u_x=0 at every node; right support spread over the last few bottom-edge nodes (x from about L-2h to L, y=0)

items.entity: bottom-right (beam end) support
items.description: The type of restraint at the beam end is not given (only 'standard MBB [17]'). The usual half-MBB uses a vertical roller; a pin adds horizontal restraint (combined with the left-edge symmetry) and allows arch-like layouts without a bottom tie.
readings: Roller: u_y=0 only
Pin: u_x=u_y=0

items.entity: unit point load at top-left node
items.description: Appendix C: 'a unit load applied at the top-left node' does not state a direction; standard MBB implies vertical. Reversing the sign changes neither the layout nor the compliance under linear elasticity.
readings: Vertical downward (-y)
Vertical upward (+y)

items.entity: physical dimensions / element size of the 144x48 domain
items.description: Only the element counts N_x x N_y = 144 x 48 are given (Appendix C). Beam length/height, element size (square assumed), half- vs full-beam wording and the units of r_min are not stated. With square Q4 elements and r_min read in element widths, this does not change the layout.
readings: Unit square elements: half-beam of 144 x 48 length units, r_min in element widths
Half-beam normalized to 3 x 1 (h = 1/48), r_min still in element widths

items.entity: plane-stress thickness
items.description: Appendix C specifies Q4 plane-stress elements but never the out-of-plane thickness; it only scales stiffness and compliance.
readings: Another uniform thickness (compliance scales as 1/t)

items.entity: Heaviside projection threshold eta_h
items.description: Sec. 5, Eq. (17): eta_h is 'either determined via bisection to enforce volume conservation across the projection or fixed to 0.5'. The text never says which option the MBB runs use. With eta_h=0.5 the volume of the projected (physical) design drifts away from 30%.
readings: eta_h found by bisection every iteration (volume-preserving projection)
eta_h fixed at 0.5

items.entity: 30% volume target - density field it constrains
items.description: Eq. (14) enforces sum v_i*rho~_i = V_0 (30%, Appendix C) on the sigmoid output before the density filter and Heaviside step. Whether the physical density used in FEA also has 30% depends on the unresolved eta_h choice and on the density filter not preserving volume at boundaries. Standard solvers constrain the physical density instead.
readings: 30% (equality) on the pre-filter sigmoid field rho~ only; physical volume may deviate
30% on the physical (filtered + projected) density rho used in FEA

items.entity: density filter radius r_min: lower bound / converged value
items.description: Table 1 bounds r_min to [1.5, 10.0], but Sec. 5.1 says r_min converges to its lower bound 'set to r_min = 2.0 to prevent checkerboard patterns'. Because r_min ends at the bound, the effective final radius is either 1.5 or 2.0 (element widths presumed).
readings: Lower bound and final r_min = 2.0
Lower bound and final r_min = 1.5

items.entity: initial SIMP penalty p^(0) and initial filter radius r_min^(0) (four-hyperparameter runs, Fig. 5)
items.description: In Fig. 5, p (bounds [1,10]) and r_min (bounds [1.5,10]) are tuned, but their starting values are never given. p=3 and r_min=2 are stated only for the 2-D (eta, beta) landscape and the standard-parameterization runs (Appendix C, C.2).
readings: p^(0)=1 (convex, continuation-like start), r_min^(0)=2.0
p^(0)=3, r_min^(0) mid-range (e.g. 4-5) decreasing toward the bound

items.entity: initial Heaviside sharpness beta^(0)
items.description: Sec. 5.1: the BOTH runs use '4 values of beta^(0)' that are never listed. beta^(0) for the standard-parameterization runs (C.2) is also missing. The bounds differ slightly too: Table 1 lower bound 0.05 vs the landscape grid starting at 0.1.
readings: beta^(0) spread over the bounds, e.g. {0.1, 1, 5, 10}
single beta^(0) = 1

items.entity: learned/final eta, beta, p (and r_min) that produced the Fig. 5c MBB design
items.description: The tuned schedules and end values appear only as curves in Fig. 5d. The text says only that beta 'remains small ... increasing only in the later stages' and that r_min reaches its bound. No final beta, p or eta numbers are reported, so a fixed-setting re-run has to read them from the figure.
readings: Use median end values read from Fig. 5d
Fixed p=3, r_min=2 with beta continuation up to the bound 15
Fixed p=3, r_min=2, beta about 1 throughout

items.entity: volume-enforcing sigmoidal projection Phi
items.description: Sec. 5: Phi is a 'parametric sigmoidal projection' that is shifted by bisection to satisfy the volume target. Its slope/temperature parameter, exact form and bisection tolerance are not given (the text defers to [14]).
readings: rho~ = logistic(x + b) with unit slope, b found by bisection
rho~ = logistic(s*(x - b)) with a steeper slope, e.g. s = 5-10

items.entity: CNN decoder upsampling layers
items.description: Appendix C.1: the dense layer outputs (N_x/8, N_y/8, 32), followed by 'five successive hidden layers' that each double the resolution 'until the output matches (N_x, N_y)'. Five doublings would give 4N_x x 4N_y; only three doublings are consistent.
readings: Five conv blocks of which only three upsample (e.g. resize factors 1,2,2,2,1)
Three blocks, each doubling the resolution
Five blocks with doubling in the first three (2,2,2,1,1)

items.entity: CNN architecture details (kernels, channels, output activation, initialization)
items.description: Appendix C.1 leaves out the convolution kernel size, channel counts per block, output activation and weight/latent initialization, deferring to [14] and its code.
readings: 5x5 kernels with channels decreasing to 1 (e.g. 128-64-32-16-1), variance-scaling weights, latent ~ N(0,1)
3x3 kernels with 32 channels in every block

items.entity: initial design: neural-network initializations / random seeds
items.description: Sec. 5.1 uses five random network initializations, plus one 'fixed initialization' for the landscape, but gives no seeds or initial values. In the CNN case the initial design is the network output, so the starting design is undetermined.
readings: Standard random initialization with seeds 0-4
Any five independent random seeds

items.entity: Adam moment coefficients (LL and UL)
items.description: Adam is used at both levels (Sec. 3, Algorithm 1), but only the learning rates, tau1/tau2 and gradient clipping are specified. beta1 and beta2 are never stated; the LL state is reset at every UL iteration.
readings: beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999 (common defaults)
Lower momentum, e.g. beta1=0.5, beta2=0.9

items.entity: total budget B_max / stopping point of BOTH MBB runs
items.description: No numerical budget is given for the MBB runs; it appears only on the x-axis of Fig. 5a. The unit is also inconsistent: Sec. 3 and App. A.1 say 'cumulative LL iterations', while Algorithm 1 adds 4t+2 per UL step and Fig. 5a counts linear solves. Because beta rises late, the stopping point affects the final design.
readings: Budget in linear solves (4t+2 per UL step) matching the Fig. 5a x-axis
Budget in cumulative LL iterations (t per UL step)
Budget equal to BO's (about 100 LL iterations per BO trial times the number of trials)

items.entity: initial LL horizon t_start
items.description: Sec. 3 says t_start is 'typically set to 1 or 2', and recommends t=2 when hyperparameters (e.g. p, eta) have no direct UL term. The value used for the MBB runs is not given; t_max=10 is stated only in general terms.
readings: t_start = 1
t_start = 2

items.entity: UL normalization constants c_ref and d_ref
items.description: Sec. 5 and Appendix C say c_ref and d_ref are 'calculated based on a random network initialization and kept fixed'. Neither their values nor the hyperparameters used to compute them are reported. They set the effective compliance/discreteness weighting that drives the tuned hyperparameters.
readings: c_ref = compliance (p=1) and d_ref = discreteness of the initial design of one random CNN init at the initial hyperparameters
Same initial design, but with compliance evaluated at the LL penalty p=3

items.entity: passive solid/void elements and padding
items.description: No passive regions or padding are mentioned for the MBB example, while the L-bracket (which uses 'the same density and projection filters') has void padding and a solid load patch. The silence presumably means none.
readings: No passive elements or padding (plain 144x48 rectangle)
Void padding layer around free edges (as in the L-bracket)
Small solid passive patch at the load/support nodes

items.entity: number of BO runs / network initializations in the comparison
items.description: Sec. 5.1 says BO is repeated with '4 random seeds and five neural network initializations per seed, giving 24 runs' (4x5=20). Appendix C.3 says '8 independent BO trials per network initialization (three initializations), giving 24'. BOTH uses 5 initializations x 4 beta^(0) = 20 runs.
readings: BO: 4 seeds x 5 network initializations (20 runs)
BO: 8 GP seeds x 3 network initializations (24 runs)

locator: Sec. 5, the MBB beam (Appendix C, Fig. 5)
